title: Ticking-Over Nesting Counter Overflow
pattern: Tracking nested resource acquisitions or read-side lock nesting using a plain, bounded integer counter without overflow checks.
why_bad: If nesting exceeds the maximum value of the integer (e.g., 255 for a `uint8_t`), the counter ticks over to zero. The next unlock statement will see the count as zero, incorrectly signaling a quiescent state and freeing active memory while nesting still exists.
detection: An integer-based nesting counter incremented without assertions or bitwise boundaries.
counterexample: Using bitwise markers (such as reserving high bits for nesting and checking for overflow).
source: Paul McKenney Appendix B.8, Quick Quiz B.21
